content: Romana's sign, also referred to as a chagoma, is a medical term that describes a unilateral, painless swelling around the eye (periorbital swelling) that occurs during the acute phase of Chagas' disease. This swelling results from conjunctival inflammation caused by contamination with the feces of the vector insect, which contains the parasitic organism Trypanosoma cruzi. While this sign is highly characteristic of Chagas' disease, it does not manifest in all patients experiencing the acute form of the disease. The term Romana's sign is named after Cecilio Romana, an Argentinian researcher who was the first to describe this clinical phenomenon.
